column1: # Expectations are separated by ";" -- see judge() in selftest.py for the forms.
# Two conventions worth keeping when adding rows:
#  * Prefer "mate<=N" over "mate=N". A shorter mate than the one published with
#    the problem is a better answer, not a failure, and pinning the exact number
#    turns every genuine improvement into a red row.
#  * Prefer a centipawn floor ("cp>=400") over a window. Evaluations of the same
#    position drift by half a pawn between runs -- the hash table is warm after
#    the mate ladder and cold without it -- so a tight window fails at random
# The first two rows are the reason this file exists: both are mates that the
# ordinary search prunes away and only the `go mate n` ladder finds.

column1: # The full-enumeration path. selftest runs --scan off everywhere else, so until
# these rows the verdict branches had no end-to-end cover at all: only the two
# headline_understates() is deliberately NOT covered from end to end. Its
# condition is "the search resolved some replies and not others", which is a
# fact about how fast the machine was, not about the position: the row tried
# here fired on 6 of 6 standalone runs and failed inside the suite, where the
# runs are back to back. A row that red-flags on load teaches the suite to be
# ignored. That rule stays covered by constructed tables in test_verdict.py,
# which is what a rule about reporting an unresolved search needs.
